title: AcmeDB: restore from a snapshot
summary: Use this when a production AcmeDB 2.x database is corrupt, dropped, or rolled to a bad state and you need a point-in-time restore from snapshots. Covers restores inside the seven-day retention window; anything older is an archive job, not this runbook. For databases over 2 TB, budget hours for the snapshot copy, not minutes.
danger: Never restore over the live data directory. Restore to a scratch path, verify with acmedb doctor, then cut over — the WAL may still be writing, and a restore on top of it corrupts both copies.
preflight: Confirm it is a data problem, not a config problem: run acmedb doctor on the live node first
Get sign-off from the on-call lead — a restore drops every write after the restore point
Check free disk: the restored copy needs roughly 1.1x the live data dir
Pick a restore point inside the seven-day snapshot retention window
Tell #acmedb-incidents the restore is starting so nobody else touches the node

phases.name: Phase 1: pick and check the snapshot

steps.do: List snapshots and choose the restore point
steps.expect: A snapshot ID whose timestamp predates the incident.

steps.do: Verify the snapshot is complete before you touch it
steps.expect: acmedb snapshot verify exits 0 and prints ok: true for every segment.

phases.name: Phase 2: restore to a scratch path

steps.do: Restore into the scratch directory, not the live one
steps.expect: restore exits 0 and the scratch dir holds a full data directory.

steps.do: Replay the WAL up to the exact restore point
Health-check the restored copy with acmedb doctor
steps.expect: Three green checks. A yellow on replication is expected — it rejoins after cutover.

steps.do: Spot-check the data you actually lost
steps.command: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE created_at > '2026-10-26';
steps.expect: Row counts match the pre-incident numbers in the incident doc. Check a few rows by hand, not just counts.

steps.do: Swap the data directories and restart
steps.command: systemctl stop acmedb && mv /var/lib/acmedb /var/lib/acmedb.bad && mv /var/lib/acmedb-restore /var/lib/acmedb && systemctl start acmedb
steps.expect: acmedb doctor goes green on the live node within a minute.

rollback: systemctl stop acmedb on the live node
Move the restored directory aside and put acmedb.bad back in place as the live data dir
systemctl start acmedb — the bad state returns, but the service is up and you can regroup

escalation.when: verify fails or replay stalls over 10 min
snapshot missing inside the retention window
doctor reports manifest corruption on the restore

lesson: We lost four hours of writes because the restore went over the live directory while the WAL was still being written, and nobody noticed until the morning.

notes.retention: Seven days is the default retention. The changelog says it is configurable and does not say how far.
notes.wal-path: In 2.0 the config key is storage.wal_path; a 1.x config silently writes the WAL somewhere you are not replaying.
